Most recent work

Jean R. Mineo, built from her Marquis Who’s Who placement

Jean R. Mineo is Executive Director of Bellforge Arts Center in Medfield, Massachusetts. The hardest thing about her record is that it is not a career of job titles, it is a single building project measured in decades. So the site is built as the project: the former Medfield State Hospital from 1896 to its closure in 2003, the town’s acquisition, then the campus itself broken down building by building: Lee Chapel, the Infirmary and the glass connector between them.

The numbers carry the credibility, so they are stated plainly rather than dressed up: a $30 million arts campus, a 300-seat venue, seventeen teaching spaces, $20.7 million of a $25 million campaign raised, groundbreaking June 2026, doors autumn 2027. Her earlier work (directing Boston Sculptors Gallery from 2006, public art curation and cultural council leadership) sits underneath as the reason she was trusted with it.

  • A project, not a CVHer authority comes from one thing she has been building for years. The site is structured as that project, with her career as the foundation under it, rather than as a reverse-chronological list.
  • Live campaign figures$20.7M of $25M is the number that makes a donor act. It is on the page, dated, and easy to update as it moves.
  • Verification, not adjectivesEvery date, figure and title on the site comes from her own published record. Nothing is asserted that cannot be checked.
  • Print stylesheetsBoard members and donors print these pages. Every site here reflows to paper with disclosures preserved.
  • Audited before releaseZero WCAG AA contrast failures, zero horizontal overflow, zero broken links, zero layout shift, checked at real viewport widths rather than eyeballed.

What is stopping the next sites

Everything on the customer sheet that can be built has been built. Fourteen names are still open, and not one of them is waiting on design or production time. Each is waiting on a single specific thing, listed below.

Waiting on one photograph 2 clients, research already done

  • Merle S. Robboy, MDSource facts written, template chosen, ready to build. His own company page and his employer's page carry no photograph of him. He appears only on doctor directories such as Healthgrades, WebMD and Vitals, which are third-party listings rather than his own published material, so their headshots are not a legitimate reference for a commercial site. One photograph he is happy to use and the site can be built the same day.
  • Allan JungSource facts written, ready to build. His company site, jungenterprise.net, carries product photographs only and no picture of him anywhere. Same position: one photograph and it goes ahead.

Waiting on a bio or a phone call 8 clients, no published placement exists

  • No press release to build fromRichard Favorito, Stan Schekall, Donald Massenburg, Ilene Fennoy, Diane Carbo, Leanne Levine, Lauren Clark, Richard Dunn. Each was searched on 24-7PressRelease by full name and again by surname alone, and none returns a placement. Their sites cannot be written from nothing, and nothing on a client site is ever invented. A short written bio from the client, or fifteen minutes on the phone with them, unblocks each one.

Waiting on a decision 4 items, minutes each

  • Ana Eugenia FerreiraHer row is struck through in red on the sheet, which everywhere else means cancelled or refunded, yet her site is live and serving. Confirm whether she stays published.
  • Andrew Charles CooperHis site is live, but he is not on the customer sheet, so there is no address on file to route his enquiries to. His email address is the only thing needed.
  • John W. FisherHis enquiry form is pointed at an address that matches no client name on file. Confirm the correct address, or that the current one is intended.
  • Dennis Ibold and Graham DavisBoth struck through in red on the sheet and locked so no build starts on them by mistake. Confirm they are cancelled for good.

Waiting on one sign-in 4 sites, four minutes

  • Four contact forms ready to correctShoemaker, Chvatal, Berry and Grimes. Corrected files are prepared, checked and sitting ready in the project folder. Uploading them needs the browser signed in to the hosting account. Sign in once and all four go up together.

Nothing above needs build time. The queue is fourteen small answers, not fourteen projects.
